findings.title: Hardcoded secret credential exposed in source
findings.body: A hardcoded token `PARTNER_TOKEN` is committed to the repository, which violates the principle of least privilege and risks accidental exposure in logs, version control, or runtime environments. Secrets must be injected via environment variables or a secure secrets manager.

findings.title: Token comparison is vulnerable to timing attacks
findings.body: The equality check `token == PARTNER_TOKEN` is vulnerable to timing attacks, allowing an attacker to guess the token by measuring response times. Use a constant-time comparison function (e.g., `secrets.compare_digest`) to mitigate this risk.
findings.suggestion:
from secrets import compare_digest
    return compare_digest(token or "", PARTNER_TOKEN)

summary.problem: The new authorization module hardcodes a secret credential and uses an unsafe comparison, introducing critical security risks.
summary.done_well: The function `can_read_private_records` is simple and focused on a single authorization check.
